subject: DPA clarifications and data handling follow-up (Orion Payments)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@orionpayments.com>
Cc: Sofia Martinez <sofia.m@orionpayments.com>
Date: 2026-07-12T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: DPA + data handling items from today's call

Thanks again for the call today — appreciated the deep dive on your payments use case. Per our discussion, attaching the current Redwood DPA (Redwood_DPA_v1.2.pdf) and a short security FAQ that addresses logging and retention. High-level recap and next steps: 

- Scope: Redwood will act as processor for customer-supplied transaction data. Customer remains controller (you confirmed).
- Data residency: we can route and store logs/embeddings to AWS regions in us-east-1 or us-west-2 for your account; we don't replicate to other regions by default.
- PII & minimization: we recommend token-level redaction at ingestion for PAN/SSNs; we can provide guidance and sample regex rules.
- Retention & logging: default logs retained 90 days; adjustable via Dedicated/private contracts.
- Breach notice: DPA specifies 72-hour notification to customer for confirmed incidents; legal can clarify specifics.

Next steps: 1) Liam — please confirm controller role and desired region; 2) we'll loop legal to answer subprocessors/breach language and provide any redlines; 3) if acceptable, I'll send for signature and schedule contract review next week.

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_v1.2.pdf (attached), security_faq.xlsx (attached)

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.ai

From: Liam O'Connor <liam@orionpayments.com>

Date: 2026-07-13T10:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: DPA + data handling items from today's call

Thanks Ben — quick clarifications so our legal and security teams can triage: 

1) Controller/Processor: Confirmed that Orion Payments is the Controller; Redwood will be Processor. Please ensure the DPA reflect that explicitly.
2) Subprocessors: we need a list of current subprocessors (hosting, monitoring, analytics) and a commitment to 30-day notice prior to adding any new subprocessors or an evergreen list in a notice portal.
3) Breach notice: our policy is 24 hours for initial notification and 72 hours for detailed report. Can Redwood meet 24-hour initial notification?
4) Data residency: we want all production data and logs to remain in us-east-1; is that configurable for hosted Dedicated accounts?
5) Logging and retention: can you confirm whether chat logs contain full plaintext inputs by default and whether there is an option to mask or not persist them?

If you can loop in legal/security with answers and any redlines, we'll review and revert.

—Liam
Liam O'Connor
Head of Integrations, Orion Payments

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@orionpayments.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>, Sofia Martinez <sofia.m@orionpayments.com>
Date: 2026-07-15T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Follow-up: DPA + data handling items from today's call

Hi Liam — thanks for the clear list. Below are clarifications and proposed edits to the DPA: 

1) Controller / Processor: We will update section 1 to state explicitly that Orion Payments is the Controller and Redwood Inference is a Processor for customer-submitted content and inference results. We'll include a short definition of 'processing' that matches the services described.

2) Subprocessors: Current subprocessors (hosting/support/monitoring) are: AWS (hosting - us-east-1), Datadog (monitoring), Sentry (error reporting), and Postgres (RDS managed by AWS). We can add a clause to provide notice of new subprocessors at least 30 days prior to onboarding, and maintain a public list at https://status.redwood.ai/subprocessors. If you prefer an absolute approval right rather than notice, let us know — that requires an enterprise contractual addendum.

3) Breach notice: Redwood's standard DPA provides for notification of confirmed incidents without undue delay and, where feasible, within 72 hours for material breaches. Operationally, our SOC/IR team will provide an initial acknowledgement within 24 hours of detection with next steps and an ETA for a full impact report. We can add language to clarify initial acknowledgment timelines while retaining 72-hour window for the full incident report.

4) Data residency: For hosted Dedicated and Private deployments, we can pin customer production data and logs to a single AWS region (us-east-1). For the hosted multi-tenant product, we can route per-customer projects to us-east-1 but cannot guarantee physical isolation unless you choose Dedicated or Private. We'll mark the DPA to show region controls and note options/costs for Dedicated.

5) Logging & retention: Default telemetry and request logs are retained for 90 days. Request/response payloads (chat logs) are persisted by default in the customer project and accessible to the customer; we provide optional redaction/masking at ingestion and a config to disable persistence. We will add explicit controls to the Security FAQ and DPA exhibit describing masking, retention configuration, and deletion APIs.

Next steps: 
- I'll attach a short redline of the DPA with the edits above and a subprocessors link.
- Ben — please confirm whether Orion prefers the 30-day notice model or approval right for new subprocessors.
- Liam/Sofia — if you confirm controller designation and us-east-1 residency, we can prepare an updated DPA for signature and surface Dedicated pricing if you want physical isolation.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
